chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The woman sees the blood while she is in a state of janabah. Should she perform ghusl from the janabah, or [is it] the ghusl of janabah and haydh [together]?' So he said: 'There has come to her what is greater than that.'

key_terms.جنابة: Janabah — the state of major ritual impurity (hadath akbar) resulting from sexual intercourse or seminal discharge, requiring ghusl
key_terms.حيض: Haydh — menstrual blood/menstruation, also causing major ritual impurity
key_terms.غسل: Ghusl — the full-body ritual bath required to remove states of major impurity

ai.seo_question: If a woman is in a state of janabah and then menstruates, does she need one or two ghusls?
ai.summary: Sa'id ibn Yasar asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about a woman who experiences menstruation while she is already in a state of janabah — whether she needs one or two separate ritual baths. The Imam's response, 'There has come to her what is greater than that,' is understood in Shia fiqh to mean that the haydh (menstruation) subsumes or supersedes the janabah, and a single ghusl of haydh is sufficient to cover both impurities, given that haydh is a more comprehensive state. This ruling reflects the Imam's concise jurisprudential method, answering practical ritual purity questions for his community.
word_analysis: in a state of janabah (sexual impurity)
